summary: Public memory return reaches Neo-Vectra through a present-day couple whose ordinary morning commute is suddenly interrupted by a recovered south-gate memory neither can fit into their shared life.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Morning rush in Neo-Vectra. The same MAN and WOMAN are clearly a present-day couple: shared coffee, one transit card between them, matching apartment keys, familiar irritation about being late. Keep the crisis embedded in an ordinary commute.
Panel 2 — The woman stops dead while still holding the man's sleeve: 'You left me at the south gate.' He looks at her, confused: 'I was standing next to you five seconds ago.'
Panel 3 — Woman: 'Not here. Before.' Man: 'What south gate?' Their present intimacy remains visible even as the recovered memory creates distance.
Panel 4 — Theo, Rae and Adrian enter the edge of the scene. Rae reaches the woman first and tells the man not to tell her she is wrong just because he cannot remember it.
Panel 5 — Theo asks, 'What do we tell her?' Rae looks at both partners rather than only the remembering woman.
Panel 6 — Rae: 'That you're both here now.' The man offers the same coffee back to the woman; she takes it automatically even while staring past him at a place that no longer exists.

Panel 7 — End on them continuing to stand together inside the rush-hour flow while the city begins filling with other small contradictions: coworkers recognizing erased uniforms, a child using an unfamiliar place-name, an older commuter crying without knowing why.
